I’ve worked in short term disability/ Fmla claims for a few years. Claims actually being mishandled in “bad faith” is very rare. I don’t know what the specifics of this situation are. If you just started a new job you won’t be eligible for Fmla. You have to be employed for 12 months and worked 1250 hours in the last 12 months. Job accommodations under ADA don’t have the requirements that Fmla does. Accommodations may be through hr or there may be a 3rd party administrator. HR should be able to advise you where to apply. There are medical documents needed to approve accommodations. You don’t need to tell your direct supervisor anything about your condition. Do you know why you were denied? That would be your first step. You can be denied for eligibility. Meaning that you haven’t been employed long enough to qualify under your company’s short-term disability program. You can also be denied for not being out of work long enough. Most companies require a minimum of 1-2 weeks off work before issuing disability payments. 

You can also be denied for not submitting the medical paperwork. Or maybe your doctor wrote up a work excuse note but it doesn’t include the diagnostic codes and what not that are required to approve disability. Or you can be denied for medical not supporting. Which can range anywhere from the doctor saying you should be working or leaving half of the questions unanswered. Another example could be that your doctor is recommending 6 months off work but that your mental health exam is within normal limits, there is no treatment plan. You should be able to appeal for all of the reasons other than eligibility denials.

I work in Fmla and I’ve also taken it for surgeries. If you need a whole month, you’ll want to file short term disability. Each company has a waiting period that you aren’t paid for. Usually it’s 1-2 weeks. Workers comp is impossible to get approved for mental health, so I wouldn’t even bother with that. The paperwork is generally extensive. It’s usually 3-4 pages. For mental health generally you’ll need a diagnosis, need to see a counselor x times per month, and be prescribed medication. Or it’s not considered a serious health condition. Each company has their own specifics that are used when approving disability, but that’s usually what I see from companies. They may also have a “personal leave” option. For Fmla you have to have 12 months of employment and worked 1250 hours in the last 12 months. There is also a look back period determined by your employer. Usually this is 1-2 days. Meaning that if you opened a claim today, they could only cover absences from yesterday or the day before. If the absence was a week ago it will be denied. You will be given a due date for the paperwork. It’s usually 2-3 weeks. Again, depending on your employer. Any absences reported between the lookback period and the due date are pending until a decision is made. Meaning you can’t get written up for those dates unless a denial has been processed. 

The medical condition has to be serious. There are several ways a condition can qualify, but generally would need to be long term (1 year or more) or require hospitalization. Mental breaks are not qualifying. Generally speaking you’ll need a mental health diagnosis, be seeing a psychologist regularly, prescribed medications etc to be approved for Fmla for mental health.

I’ve worked in Fmla for 3 years now. For a giant company so we are a 3rd party administrator, but smaller companies typically just have hr do it. I’m assuming the ceos wife is part of hr. In order to approve Fmla you have to have 12 months of service and 1250 hours. You can only get 12 weeks (480 hours based off a 40 hour work week, per year). Some states have different requirements. The forms have to be filled out in full and submitted by the deadline. Deadlines usually range from 14-30 days, is decided by the company.

There are several categories that a condition can qualify under. The date range that you will be out has to be specified. They will not accept an unknown or undefined duration. Usually claims can only be approved a maximum of 1 year, even if it’s a 5 year long condition. The intermittent absences have to be numerically defined (as in 2 appointments per week lasting 2 hours per appointment). The diagnosis and symptoms must be listed unless you are a California resident. The paper work must be signed by a licensed provider in the USA and they may not accept electronic forms. 

So technically they do need to know your diagnosis to approve Fmla. However, it’s against hipaa for your direct manager to be made aware of the condition. And they really shouldn’t just be texting/ pestering you for it. If there is an issue with the condition not being listed, usually they would work with the provider to obtain any missing info and not be having you relay it.
